Schoeller Diagram

Source: R/plotting.R
schoeller_plot.Rd

Creates a Schoeller diagram for comparing major-ion chemistry among groundwater or surface water samples.

schoeller_plot(df, ...)

# S3 method for class 'data.frame'
schoeller_plot(df, location, analyte, result, unit, date, ...)

# S3 method for class 'env_schema'
schoeller_plot(
  df,
  calcium = "Calcium, dissolved",
  magnesium = "Magnesium, dissolved",
  sodium = "Sodium, dissolved",
  potassium = "Potassium, dissolved",
  chloride = "Chloride, total",
  sulfate = "Sulfate, total",
  alkalinity = "Alkalinity, total (lab)",
  analyte_matching = c("exact", "strict", "normalized"),
  facet_var = c("location", "date"),
  title = NULL,
  lwt = 1
)

Arguments

df

A data frame or `env_schema` object.

...

Additional arguments passed to methods.

location

Location identifier column.

analyte

Analyte column.

result

Analytical result column.

unit

Reporting unit column.

date

Sample date column.

calcium

Calcium analyte.

magnesium

Magnesium analyte.

sodium

Sodium analyte.

potassium

Potassium analyte.

chloride

Chloride analyte.

sulfate

Sulfate analyte.

alkalinity

Alkalinity analyte.

analyte_matching

Analyte matching strategy. One of `"exact"`, `"strict"`, or `"normalized"`.

facet_var

Faceting variable. One of `"location"` or `"date"`.

title

Optional plot title.

lwt

Line width.

Value

A ggplot object.

Details

`schoeller_plot()` is an S3 generic that supports both raw data frames and `env_schema` objects.

For data frames, environmental column mappings must be supplied. For `env_schema` objects, mapped schema fields are used automatically.

For data frames, `schoeller_plot()` first converts the supplied data to an `env_schema` object using the specified column mappings and then dispatches to [schoeller_plot.env_schema()].

Schoeller diagrams display major-ion concentrations on a logarithmic scale and are commonly used to compare water chemistry among locations and sampling events.

Major-ion concentrations are converted to milliequivalents per liter (meq/L) and plotted as connected profiles across standard hydrochemical ion categories.

Sodium and potassium are combined into a single `"Na + K"` axis following conventional Schoeller diagram practice.

Missing analytes are permitted and omitted from the resulting profile.

For `env_schema` objects, analyte, result, unit, date, and location fields are determined from schema mappings.

Analyte Matching

exact

Uses analyte names exactly as reported.

strict

Applies text normalization while preserving analytical distinctions such as dissolved versus total fractions.

normalized

Resolves analyte aliases to canonical analyte names using package analyte metadata.

Faceting

If `facet_var = "location"`, each location is displayed in a separate panel and sample events are drawn as individual profiles.

If `facet_var = "date"`, each sampling event is displayed in a separate panel and locations are drawn as individual profiles.

Validation

Input data are validated for:

  • analyte resolution;

  • supported analytical units;

  • major-ion chemistry availability;

  • successful conversion to milliequivalents.
